summary: Tested new EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED feature flag + admin endpoints (/admin/verify-user, /admin/auth-config) across both flag states. New test file test_email_verification_flag.py (16 tests) — ALL PASS. Env-var toggle + supervisor restart validated. Flag correctly restored to 'false' at end. The pre-existing test_email_verification.py suite now has 5 failures because it was written assuming strict mode — those failures are EXPECTED behavioral changes, not regressions in the new code; the tests themselves need to be updated to be flag-aware.

minor.issue: 5 pre-existing tests (TestRegister, TestLoginUnverified, TestVerifyEmail.test_verify_valid_token_then_reuse, TestResend.test_resend_verified_email, TestResend.test_resend_cooldown_429) now fail because they assume flag=true. When flag=false, register auto-issues JWT + email_verified=true, so no verification tokens are created, breaking the resend/verify test paths. Not a code bug — the tests need to force flag=true in a module fixture (or be split like test_email_verification_flag.py).

action_items: Update /app/backend/tests/test_email_verification.py to explicitly set EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED=true in a module-scoped fixture (with restart + restore), or move flag-specific assertions into test_email_verification_flag.py. Currently the file assumes strict mode and fails silently when the env flag is off.

Consider extracting the _email_verification_required() helper into a shared module — it is duplicated inline in admin.py (auth-config endpoint) using a slightly different `_os` import alias. Minor DRY nit.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: `import os` placed at line 102 (after functions using os) — works because Python evaluates on call, but visually messy. Move to top-level imports.
admin.py: /admin/verify-user + /admin/auth-config both re-implement the flag-reading logic instead of importing `_email_verification_required` from routers.auth — leads to drift risk.

No rate-limit / audit-log on /admin/verify-user — since it bypasses the primary security check (email verification), consider logging every use to a dedicated audit collection (currently only a logger.info line).
/admin/auth-config leaks whether RESEND_API_KEY is set — fine for admins, but ensure the require_admin dependency truly enforces admin (verified: it does).
EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED read via os.environ every request — fine performance-wise, but ensure new env vars are respected after supervisor restart (verified in tests).

success_rate.backend: 100% on new flag suite (16/16); pre-existing test_email_verification.py: 5 failures caused by env-flag now being false (not a code regression)

context_for_next_testing_agent: New flag-toggle test file at /app/backend/tests/test_email_verification_flag.py covers flag=false (register auto-issues JWT, login without 403, admin verify-user) + flag=true (register requires verification, login 403, verify-email regression). The env flag is auto-restored to 'false' at test-module teardown so beta users stay unblocked.
